clue.text: Each round number in counterfeit has been cut — it's a doddle

parts.note: each costs so much apiece, i.e. per item
a round shape resembles the letter O

indicators.note: the number is placed within the word for counterfeit, which has been cut open for it

parts.note: counterfeit means fake
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A forger finds that slicing up a counterfeit coin each time is easy work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' and 'number' read like coin talk; they give O and the Roman numeral C, which goes inside FAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for a task that is very easy to do.

clue.text: Accumulation has an unkind sound

indicators.note: the clue says the words are what is heard, so a soundalike is wanted

parts.note: an unkind person is a cruel one, so 'a cruel'

explanation.surface: Piling things up makes a harsh noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an accumulation is a gradual build-up, as interest builds on savings.

clue.text: Trendy dream of early days

parts.note: what is trendy is in
to dream of something is to fancy it

explanation.surface: A fashionable fantasy of one's youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the earliest period of life, or of anything, is its babyhood.

clue.text: Plods unsteadily into prison, perhaps, with a snap

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the word for a prison room

parts.note: a cell is one example of a prison

indicators.note: walking unsteadily, the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A policeman staggers into a jail with a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plods' suggests a police officer (PC Plod) walking unsteadily; here it is only letters to shuffle, and 'a snap' is a spell of weather, not a photo.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a brief spell of cold weather is called a cold snap.

clue.text: Explorer or conspirator doing porridge, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken, giving a soundalike

parts.note: porridge is made from oats

explanation.surface: A traveller or a plotter is serving time in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing porridge' is British slang for serving a prison sentence, but here porridge is just food. Lawrence Oates was on Scott's Antarctic expedition; Titus Oates invented the Popish Plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawrence Oates was a polar explorer and Titus Oates a plotter, both famous bearers of the surname.

clue.text: Petals would be a natural result when on line

indicators.note: the answer would become the longer word when a line is added to it, so the line is taken off

parts.note: a corollary is a consequence that follows naturally
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Flowers would be what naturally follows if put on a railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Botany: the corolla is the whorl of petals forming the inner envelope of a flower.

clue.text: Marsh plant family gets award for hero raised

parts.note: one's family are one's kin
GC is the George Cross, a British award for heroism
something raised is up

explanation.surface: Relatives receive a medal for a brave person's elevation.
explanation.walkthrough: The George Cross is a British medal for gallantry, abbreviated GC.
explanation.definitionFit: The marsh marigold, a yellow-flowered wetland species, is also called this.

clue.text: Fools dine at folly and get done in

parts.note: a pair of fools is two asses, ass and ass

indicators.note: folly suggests foolish disorder, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Idiots dining at a pleasure-house come to a sticky end.
explanation.walkthrough: A folly is also an ornamental building, the surface's venue; as indicator it turns DINE AT into INATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: to be done in is to be killed, especially as a public figure murdered.

clue.text: A large quantity — of sherry drunk?

definitions.meaning: as much as a big bag holds
sack is an old word for sherry, so one full of it would be full of sack

explanation.definitionFit: A bagful is a large amount; and sack was the Elizabethan name for a sweet white wine.

clue.text: Harsh rule proceeded between semi- and American cities

indicators.note: the verb sits between the half city and the American city
semi- means half, so only half of the word city is kept

parts.note: the plural covers both cities, a city and an American city
an American city here is NY, New York
to have proceeded is to have run

explanation.surface: Oppressive government moved from semi-urban areas to American metropolises.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'cities' serves both halves of the clue: half of one city and an American one, with the verb in between.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: oppressive, cruel government by a despot is harsh rule.

clue.text: Pull with ease, say, and write aimlessly in American

parts.note: to yank is to pull sharply

indicators.note: say signals a word spoken aloud: the word sounds like two letters E

parts.note: the word heard as E's, a pair of the letter
to doodle is to scribble idly

explanation.surface: Tug easily, and scribble without purpose, in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The song title doubles as a name for an American, as in the Revolutionary War tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickname: Yankee Doodle is a jocular term for an American, from the old song.

clue.text: One of five when expert in philosophy

parts.note: a quin is one of quintuplets, so a quin
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A quintuplet who happens to be a philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Aquinas was the great medieval Italian philosopher and theologian of scholasticism.

clue.text: Reportedly foolish trick with chips?

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so a soundalike

parts.note: a foolish trick is a silly con

explanation.surface: A rumoured daft scam involving gambling chips.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: microchips are made from this semiconductor element, hence the question mark.

clue.text: See 19
Treatment for payees is a doddle

indicators.note: the letters are given a treatment, worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Paying people what they are owed is simple.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something said to be very simple to do, like a doddle.

clue.text: Images showing card with number removed from 1 down wrongly

parts.note: a SIM card goes in a mobile phone

indicators.note: the letters left are arranged wrongly, i.e. shuffled

parts.note: the answer to 1 down is accrual
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Pictures display a card after a figure was wrongly taken off a ledger entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed from' is part of the composite signal: the hundred comes out of the 1 down answer and 'wrongly' scrambles what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: simulacra are likenesses or representations of things, often shadowy ones.

clue.text: Expert probing generous number finds it's a doddle

indicators.note: the expert goes deep into the word for generous

parts.note: noble can mean magnanimous or generous
a pro is an expert
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A specialist examining a large figure says it is easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: said of a task that causes no difficulty at all.

clue.text: Final notice in search for upright character

indicators.note: the notice is placed inside the word for search

parts.note: to pry is to search inquisitively
an obit is an obituary, the last notice anyone gets

explanation.surface: Looking for a person of integrity in a death notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: probity is honesty and moral uprightness.

clue.text: Opening for gold providing diamonds

parts.note: or is heraldic gold
providing means if
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A hole for gold, provided there are diamonds too.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an orifice is an opening, such as a mouth or vent.

clue.text: Drama of 2 etc is a doddle

parts.note: 2 down is infancy, so belonging to infancy and so on is a child's
a drama is a play

explanation.surface: A play about early life is easy.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' refers to the answer at 2 down, INFANCY; the 'etc' extends it to childhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a task that a youngster could do, so very easy.

clue.text: Go round with needle

definitions.meaning: to go round something is to encircle it
the navigational instrument has a magnetised pointer

explanation.definitionFit: To encompass is to circle around; and the navigator's instrument has a pointing needle.

clue.text: Caliph in parliament with lost leader like 11

indicators.note: the caliph is placed inside the reduced parliament
the parliament has lost its first letter

parts.note: the witan was the Anglo-Saxon council or parliament
Ali was the fourth caliph of Islam

explanation.surface: A Muslim ruler sits in an assembly that has lost its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like 11' points to the philosopher at 11 across, who was Italian. The witan was the Anglo-Saxon king's council.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Aquinas was born near Aquino in the Kingdom of Sicily, so of that nationality.

clue.text: Smith falsely accepting honour for 11's ideas

indicators.note: the shuffled name takes the honour inside it
a false arrangement of the letters is wanted

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A man named Smith, under false pretences, takes a decoration for a philosopher's teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: The 11 in the definition is the philosopher at 11 across; the doctrine named after him is built here.
explanation.definitionFit: The philosophy of Thomas Aquinas and his followers is named after his first name.

clue.text: Holder of revenue for motorway is the Queen

parts.note: M stands for motorway in British road names
taken as written
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The keeper of the taxes for the road is the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hoards money and will not spend it holds on to income.

clue.text: Chimney breast's opening in the past brings back trouble

parts.note: lum is Scottish and northern English for chimney

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A chimney breast's opening in olden times causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brings back trouble' looks like history returning; 'back trouble' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is pain in the muscles and joints of the lower back.

clue.text: Welshman is telling fibs to the press

parts.note: Dai is a typical Welsh male name
to tell fibs is to lie, so he lies

explanation.surface: A man from Wales is lying to journalists.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective: daily newspapers are the dailies, part of the press.

clue.text: Alaric strangely keeping his name in his head?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters hold the abbreviation inside
the letters are arranged strangely

explanation.surface: The Gothic king Alaric oddly keeps his own name in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' turns ALARIC into CRAIAL; 'keeping' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything within the skull is of the cranium, the head.

clue.text: Dreamy work for doctor being informed case was a doddle?

definitions.text: being informed case was a doddle?

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: Dr Watson is Sherlock Holmes's companion

explanation.surface: A dreamy piece of writing for a doctor, told that solving the case was easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' turns DREAMY into MYDEAR. Holmes is popularly quoted as saying 'Elementary, my dear Watson'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is what Holmes is famously supposed to say to his friend when telling him a case was elementary.
